title: Absolutely MASSIVE news...
description:
AMC just launched Leawood Films, an indie distribution label for movies that are fully financed or already completed by their filmmakers, and the key detail is that filmmakers keep their IP and downstream revenue. That is the thing independents have never been able to buy: placement in front of people who already go there, without surrendering ownership to get it.

The hardest problem in independent anything is not visibility for its own sake. It's getting your work into the places people already go, in a financially viable way. That's why creators sell their rights off. They're not buying a studio, they're buying distribution, and they overpay for it with ownership. We solved the same problem in publishing through our Hachette deal, because Barnes and Noble, Target, Walmart and the international market do not open to you directly no matter how good your book is.

Caveats included: no titles until 2027 or 2028, AMC carries about $4 billion in debt, and they tried this once before with Open Road Films.

title: The TRUTH About Black Characters & Creators | The Lanterns Effect
description:
I haven't watched Lanterns and I'm not reviewing it. I want to talk about the conversation around it: why black characters in mainstream entertainment so often lead with hardship, why that's become predictable enough to be boring, and what it costs the characters themselves.

My character Isom is named after my great-great-great-grandfather, Isom, who was born a slave and died a property owner. Knowing that history is part of why I write the way I do. Isom and Sydnee Bloodruth are black characters, but being black is not their defining trait, because if you want people to stay with a character for years, they have to be someone you relate to first.

There's also a real pressure on creators here, and it isn't only coming from audiences. The people funding this material expect a certain framing, and creators know what gets them called a sellout. I've been called worse for saying original characters should be interesting first, while running a company whose lead character is among the best selling black characters in independent comics by actual sales.
